name: A high-bandwidth implant is approved for medical use

status_basis.text: Sample. Implants are in small trials, but none is approved for general medical use.
status_basis.quote: Sample quote: all participants remain enrolled in an investigational trial.

summary.text: Sample. Approval is the step from a handful of trial participants to anyone a doctor prescribes it for.

success_criterion.text: Sample. A regulator in a major market approves an implant with at least 1,000 channels for routine clinical use.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Long-term safety data: regulators want years of evidence that implants stay safe and keep working.

forecasts.quote: Sample quote: we anticipate approval between 2029 and 2032.
Sample quote: most respondents expected approval in 2030 or 2031.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. A fast-track designation from a major regulator.

would_move_later.text: Sample. A serious safety incident in an ongoing trial.

name: A non-invasive headset decodes text at typing speed

status_basis.text: Sample. Non-invasive decoding only works for short, constrained phrases.

summary.text: Sample. If people could type by thinking, without surgery, high-bandwidth interfaces would reach far more of them.

success_criterion.text: Sample. 40 words per minute of free text with no implant, in a peer-reviewed study.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Signal quality through the skull.

forecasts.quote: Sample quote: non-invasive free-text decoding at typing speed looks achievable by 2028 to 2030.
Sample quote: the median answer for free-text decoding in everyday use, outside the lab, was 2042 to 2045.

basis.text: Sample. These two forecasts are about different things. The survey asked about decoding in everyday use outside the lab, which is a much harder target than our criterion of a peer-reviewed study, so we don't count it as disagreement.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. A big jump in non-invasive signal quality, for example from new kinds of sensor.

would_move_later.text: Sample. Results showing that decoding accuracy doesn't hold up outside the lab.

name: BCIs measurably help people keep economic agency

status_basis.text: Sample. No study has tried to measure this.

summary.text: Sample. The claim that BCIs could keep human work worth paying for as AI improves. Of the BCI milestones, this is the one that bears directly on the Intelligence Curse.

success_criterion.text: Sample. Not defined yet. The proposals we've found don't say what success would look like.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Unclear. It may not be technical at all.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. A proposal that spells out how BCI users would stay competitive, and what to measure.

would_move_later.text: Sample. We haven't found anything specific yet.

name: A neuromorphic chip matches GPUs on energy per task

status_basis.text: Sample. The results so far are on narrow benchmarks.
status_basis.quote: Sample quote: two independent groups reproduced the energy result on the same benchmark.

achieved_in_basis.text: Sample. First shown on a standard benchmark in 2024.
achieved_in_basis.quote: Sample quote: in 2024 the chip first matched GPU energy per inference on the benchmark.

summary.text: Sample. Brain-inspired hardware is already efficient on some tasks, though that doesn't tell us whether it helps alignment.

success_criterion.text: Sample. Equal or lower energy per inference than a contemporary GPU on a standard benchmark.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Software and training tools hold it back more than the chips do.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. Nothing can bring it earlier, since it has already happened.

would_move_later.text: Sample. A failed replication on broader benchmarks.

name: Brain-like training shows a measurable alignment benefit

status_basis.text: Sample. The case has been argued but not tested.
status_basis.quote: Sample quote: none of this has been tested empirically yet.

summary.text: Sample. The step where brain-inspired AI turns out to be easier to align than other AI.

success_criterion.text: Sample. A brain-inspired system beats a matched conventional system on a standard alignment evaluation, and an independent group replicates the result.

main_bottleneck.text: Sample. Nobody agrees on which alignment evaluation would count.

basis.text: Sample. We start at 2035, later than the early-2030s forecast, because that forecast assumes an agreed alignment benchmark will exist and none does yet. We won't set an end date until there's a first result.

forecasts.quote: Sample quote: I'd expect a first clear result between 2030 and 2033.
Sample quote: the median answer was 2050 to 2060.
Sample quote: I don't think brain-like training will ever give a measurable alignment benefit.

disagreement_note.text: Sample. One researcher expects first results in the early 2030s, the survey median is about twenty years later, and a skeptic says it will never happen. Our range is a judgment call that doesn't settle the disagreement, so the badge stays up.

would_move_earlier.text: Sample. An agreed alignment benchmark that brain-inspired systems can be tested on.

would_move_later.text: Sample. Evidence that brain-like learning makes values harder to inspect.

artificial_minds_questions.text: Sample. If the system learns the way brains do, could it also have experiences that matter morally?

name: A human brain emulation reproduces relevant behavior in controlled tests

status_basis.text: Not demonstrated for a human brain. Timing is unclear.

summary.text: In controlled tests, a working emulation would have to reproduce relevant behavior, and do it reliably.

success_criterion.text: A working emulation reproduces relevant behavior under controlled tests.

main_bottleneck.text: Scanning, functional modeling, simulation fidelity and validation.

would_move_earlier.text: We haven't assessed what would bring this forward.

would_move_later.text: We haven't assessed what would push this back.

name: An emulation behaves stably and reproducibly across relevant tasks

summary.text: Across relevant tasks, the emulation's behavior has to hold steady and its results have to be reproducible.

success_criterion.text: Stable, reproducible behavior across relevant tasks.

main_bottleneck.text: The functional requirements and the validation standards are both unknown.

would_move_earlier.text: We haven't assessed what would bring this forward.

would_move_later.text: We haven't assessed what would push this back.

name: A defensible welfare and consent framework exists before any emulation is created

summary.text: A framework for welfare and consent would need to be in place, and defensible, before anyone creates an emulation.

success_criterion.text: A defensible welfare and consent framework exists before any emulation is created.

main_bottleneck.text: Moral status, consent, identity and welfare safeguards are all unresolved.

would_move_earlier.text: We haven't assessed what would bring this forward.

would_move_later.text: We haven't assessed what would push this back.

name: Cost and infrastructure allow controlled research or deployment

summary.text: Manufacture, compute and data have to get cheap enough, and the infrastructure has to exist, for controlled research or deployment to be possible.

success_criterion.text: Cost and infrastructure allow controlled research or deployment.

main_bottleneck.text: Data acquisition, compute, storage and the cost of emulation.

would_move_earlier.text: We haven't assessed what would bring this forward.

would_move_later.text: We haven't assessed what would push this back.

name: A cost-benefit case holds up without exploitative labor conditions

summary.text: Someone would have to show that emulation is worth what it costs without relying on exploitative labor conditions.

success_criterion.text: A cost-benefit case is demonstrated without exploitative labor conditions.

main_bottleneck.text: The cost curve is unknown, and so is the value of emulated labor.

would_move_earlier.text: We haven't assessed what would bring this forward.

would_move_later.text: We haven't assessed what would push this back.

name: Clear legal authorization and safeguards exist

summary.text: Emulation would have to be clearly allowed by law or by regulators, with safeguards in place.

success_criterion.text: Clear legal authorization and safeguards exist.

main_bottleneck.text: Legal status, consent, copying and liability are unresolved.

would_move_earlier.text: We haven't assessed what would bring this forward.

would_move_later.text: We haven't assessed what would push this back.

name: Independent oversight and legitimate authorization processes exist

summary.text: Emulation would need someone independent watching over it, and legitimate processes for authorizing it.

success_criterion.text: Independent oversight and legitimate authorization processes exist.

main_bottleneck.text: Public trust, oversight and moral controversy.

would_move_earlier.text: We haven't assessed what would bring this forward.

would_move_later.text: We haven't assessed what would push this back.

name: Access and returns reach beyond a narrow group

summary.text: If anyone claims WBE gives equitable or broad access, then the technology and its returns have to reach beyond a narrow group.

success_criterion.text: Access and returns aren't restricted to a narrow group.

main_bottleneck.text: Ownership, access to compute and concentration of power.

would_move_earlier.text: We haven't assessed what would bring this forward.

would_move_later.text: We haven't assessed what would push this back.
